raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Quantized rollout (`rollout.quantization.linear/moe=FP8_BLOCK`) combined with an FP8 KV cache (`+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`) makes vLLM generate garbage. This PR resets the attention q/k/v/prob scales to 1.0 after every quantized refit when the rollout quant config has no `kv_cache_scheme`. Each mode works alone; only the combination breaks.

Root cause (checked in vLLM 0.29 and 0.32):

1. verl's compressed-tensors rollout config sets `kv_cache_scheme: None`, but vLLM still attaches a `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod` to every `Attention` layer.
2. Its `create_weights` registers `q/k/v_scale` placeholders initialized to 1.0. `load_format="dummy"` overwrites them with its seeded uniform values (all -7.5e-4 here). Unlike `KVCacheScaleParameter`, these placeholders set no `dummy_weight_value`.
3. `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading` adopts the loaded placeholders as the live `_q/_k/_v_scale` (and the `_float` copies). Unlike `BaseKVCacheMethod`, it has no "not in the checkpoint → 1.0" fallback. The dummy load also randomizes `_prob_scale`.
4. verl's refit sends no attention scales and re-processes only the linear/MoE layers, so the random scales are never corrected. With `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, FA3 then quantizes Q/K/V with a scale of -7.5e-4.

The fix adds `reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model)` to `process_quanted_weights_after_loading`. For every layer whose quant method is a `BaseKVCacheMethod` and whose quant config has no `kv_cache_scheme`, it calls vLLM's own `set_default_quant_scales(layer, register_buffer=False)` under `torch.no_grad()`. The `no_grad` is needed because vLLM <= 0.29 keeps the scales as the grad-requiring placeholder Parameters. Configs that do carry a `kv_cache_scheme` are left untouched. With `kv_cache_dtype=auto` the scales are unused, so the reset is a no-op in effect.

Not a duplicate: open PRs touching FP8 KV cache or KV scales were searched (queries below). #4435 adds an FP8 KV cache feature on the older FSDP path with per-step scale recalibration in `vllm_fp8_utils.py`; it does not touch the compressed-tensors refit path changed here (`vllm_quant_utils.py`, added by #8287). No open PR resets these scales. This PR does not add an FP8 KV cache option; it only stops the existing `engine_kwargs` passthrough from producing garbage with quantized rollout.

AI assistance: this PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reproduced the bug, reviewed every changed line, and ran the tests below myself.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+kv_cache_dtype , https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+%22kv+cache+scale%22 , https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+kv_cache_scheme
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

**Unit test** (new, `tests/utils/test_vllm_kv_cache_scale_reset_on_cpu.py`; loads `vllm_quant_utils` by path against stub vLLM modules, so it runs in the CPU CI). It covers four cases:

- scales stored as buffers (vLLM 0.32) and as grad-requiring Parameters (vLLM 0.29) are both reset;
- a config with a `kv_cache_scheme` keeps its scales;
- layers without a KV cache method are ignored;
- `process_quanted_weights_after_loading` performs the reset.

```
pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_kv_cache_scale_reset_on_cpu.py   # 5 passed; all 5 fail without the fix
pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_*_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py   # 56 passed
pre-commit run --files verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py tests/utils/test_vllm_kv_cache_scale_reset_on_cpu.py   # passed
```

**GPU repro on verl main + vLLM 0.32.0** (locked env, 1×H20, Qwen3-0.6B). Setup: dummy load with verl's `FP8_BLOCK` compressed-tensors config, then a refit of the real BF16 weights through `CompressedTensorsWeightQuantizer` → `prepare_quanted_weights_for_loading` → `model.load_weights` → `process_quanted_weights_after_loading`. Then greedy decoding of "The capital of France is":

| KV cache | fix | layer-0 q/k/v/prob scale after refit | prompt log-probs | greedy output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto (BF16) | – | 1.0 | -12.56, -0.50, -3.58, -0.37 | " Paris. The capital of France is also …" |
| fp8_e4m3 | no | -7.46e-4 | -11.23, -21.75, -17.03, -27.64 | "-------\n-------\n-------\n…" |
| fp8_e4m3 | yes | 1.0 | -12.85, -0.55, -3.87, -0.35 | " Paris. The capital of France is also …" |

Before the fix, all 28/28 attention layers carry the dummy scales after a dummy load; after `process_quanted_weights_after_loading`, 0/28 do.

**End-to-end** (earlier verl main with the same fix, vLLM 0.29). Setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, Megatron TE blockwise FP8 training + FP8_BLOCK rollout + `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`, DAPO-Math, 8×H20.

- Train-vs-rollout `k3_kl` probe (8 prompts × 4, 2K responses): NaN before the fix, 0.0066 after. For reference, BF16 gives 0.00085 and FP8_BLOCK without FP8 KV gives 0.0029.
- AIME-2024 at step 0: 0.0 before the fix, 4.6% after (BF16: 5.4%).
- The fixed run trained 100 steps stably; `k3_kl` over the last 20 steps was 0.0029.

### API and Usage Example

No API or config change. FP8 KV cache with quantized rollout now works through the existing passthrough:

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization.linear=FP8_BLOCK \
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization.moe=FP8_BLOCK \
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3
```

The KV cache then runs with q/k/v scales of 1.0 (uncalibrated), the same as an FP8 KV cache on an unquantized model.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`: new `reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model)`, called from `process_quanted_weights_after_loading` (after the linear/MoE post-processing, before the ROCm `wo_a` cache rebuild). It returns early if the vLLM symbols are missing (older vLLM).
- `tests/utils/test_vllm_kv_cache_scale_reset_on_cpu.py`: CPU unit test.

Out of scope:

- Calibrated KV scales: exporting per-layer `k_scale`/`v_scale` through a `kv_cache_scheme` on each refit. A user-provided `config_file` with a `kv_cache_scheme` keeps the dummy scales today, because verl does not export KV scales. This PR leaves that path unchanged.
- SGLang: not checked.

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). Not needed for the fix; FP8 KV cache usage and results for `docs/low_precision/fp8.md` will follow in a separate PR.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. The `*_on_cpu.py` test is picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`.

Setup: dummy load with verl's `FP8_BLOCK` compressed-tensors config, then a refit of the real BF16 weights through `CompressedTensorsWeightQuantizer` → `prepare_quanted_weights_for_loading` → `model.load_weights` → `process_quanted_weights_after_loading`. Then greedy decoding of "The capital of France is":

| KV cache | fix | layer-0 q/k/v/prob scale after refit | prompt log-probs | greedy output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto (BF16) | – | 1.0 | -12.56, -0.50, -3.58, -0.37 | " Paris. The capital of France is also …" |
| fp8_e4m3 | no | -7.46e-4 | -11.23, -21.75, -17.03, -27.64 | "-------\n-------\n-------\n…" |
| fp8_e4m3 | yes | 1.0 | -12.85, -0.55, -3.87, -0.35 | " Paris. The capital of France is also …" |

Before the fix, all 28/28 attention layers carry the dummy scales after a dummy load; after `process_quanted_weights_after_loading`, 0/28 do.

**End-to-end** (earlier verl main with the same fix, vLLM 0.29). Setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, Megatron TE blockwise FP8 training + FP8_BLOCK rollout + `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`, DAPO-Math, 8×H20.

- Train-vs-rollout `k3_kl` probe (8 prompts × 4, 2K responses): NaN before the fix, 0.0066 after. For reference, BF16 gives 0.00085 and FP8_BLOCK without FP8 KV gives 0.0029.
- AIME-2024 at step 0: 0.0 before the fix, 4.6% after (BF16: 5.4%).
- The fixed run trained 100 steps stably; `k3_kl` over the last 20 steps was 0.0029.

### API and Usage Example

No API or config change. FP8 KV cache with quantized rollout now works through the existing passthrough:

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization.linear=FP8_BLOCK \
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization.moe=FP8_BLOCK \
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3
```

The KV cache then runs with q/k/v scales of 1.0 (uncalibrated), the same as an FP8 KV cache on an unquantized model.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`: new `reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model)`, called from `process_quanted_weights_after_loading` (after the linear/MoE post-processing, before the ROCm `wo_a` cache rebuild). It returns early if the vLLM symbols are missing (older vLLM).
- `tests/utils/test_vllm_kv_cache_scale_reset_on_cpu.py`: CPU unit test.

Out of scope:

- Calibrated KV scales: exporting per-layer `k_scale`/`v_scale` through a `kv_cache_scheme` on each refit. A user-provided `config_file` with a `kv_cache_scheme` keeps the dummy scales today, because verl does not export KV scales. This PR leaves that path unchanged.

+"""A quantized refit must leave the attention q/k/v/prob scales at 1.0 when the config has no KV scheme.
+
+verl's compressed-tensors rollout config sets ``kv_cache_scheme: None``, yet vLLM still gives every
+attention layer a ``CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod``. ``load_format="dummy"`` fills its scale
+placeholders with random values and the method adopts them as the live scales, so with
+``kv_cache_dtype="fp8"`` the rollout quantized Q/K/V with a scale of about -7.5e-4 and produced
+garbage (NaN rollout log-probs). Nothing in the refit re-processed the attention layers.
+
+``vllm_quant_utils`` is loaded by path against stub vLLM modules, so these run without vLLM. The
+stub ``set_default_quant_scales`` mirrors vLLM's ``register_buffer=False`` branch.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import sys
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+_DUMMY_SCALE = -7.5e-4  # what vLLM's dummy loader wrote into every scale (seeded uniform(-1e-3, 1e-3))
+_SCALES = ("_q_scale", "_k_scale", "_v_scale", "_prob_scale")
+
+
+class _BaseKVCacheMethod:
+    def __init__(self, quant_config):
+        self.quant_config = quant_config
+
+
+class _CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod(_BaseKVCacheMethod):
+    pass
+
+
+def _set_default_quant_scales(layer, register_buffer=False):
+    assert not register_buffer
+    for name in _SCALES:
+        getattr(layer, name).fill_(1.0)
+    layer._q_scale_float = layer._k_scale_float = layer._v_scale_float = layer._prob_scale_float = 1.0
+    layer._k_scale_cpu = torch.tensor(1.0)
+    layer._v_scale_cpu = torch.tensor(1.0)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def quant_utils(monkeypatch):
+    attention = types.ModuleType("vllm.model_executor.layers.attention.attention")
+    attention.set_default_quant_scales = _set_default_quant_scales
+    kv_cache = types.ModuleType("vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.kv_cache")
+    kv_cache.BaseKVCacheMethod = _BaseKVCacheMethod
+    # A bare package stub, so ``verl.utils.vllm.vllm_fp*_utils`` load from their files without
+    # running ``verl/utils/vllm/__init__.py``, which imports vLLM.
+    package = types.ModuleType("verl.utils.vllm")
+    package.__path__ = [str(_REPO_ROOT / "verl/utils/vllm")]
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, attention.__name__, attention)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, kv_cache.__name__, kv_cache)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, package.__name__, package)
+
+    before = set(sys.modules)
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+        "vllm_quant_utils_under_test", _REPO_ROOT / "verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py"
+    )
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    yield module
+    # Drop the submodules loaded under the stub package so later tests import the real package.
+    for name in set(sys.modules) - before:
+        if name.startswith("verl.utils.vllm."):
+            sys.modules.pop(name, None)
+
+
+def _attention_layer(kv_cache_scheme=None, as_parameters=False, method_cls=_CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod):
+    """An attention layer as vLLM leaves it after a dummy load with a compressed-tensors config."""
+    layer = nn.Module()
+    for name in _SCALES:
+        value = torch.tensor(_DUMMY_SCALE)
+        if as_parameters:
+            # vLLM <= 0.29 rebinds ``_k_scale`` etc. to the placeholder ``nn.Parameter``s, which require grad.
+            setattr(layer, name, nn.Parameter(value))
+        else:
+            layer.register_buffer(name, value)
+        setattr(layer, f"{name}_float", _DUMMY_SCALE)
+    layer.quant_method = method_cls(SimpleNamespace(kv_cache_scheme=kv_cache_scheme))
+    return layer
+
+
+def _scales(layer):
+    return [getattr(layer, name).item() for name in _SCALES] + [
+        layer._q_scale_float,
+        layer._k_scale_float,
+        layer._v_scale_float,
+        layer._prob_scale_float,
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("as_parameters", [False, True], ids=["buffers", "grad_parameters"])
+def test_resets_scales_without_kv_cache_scheme(quant_utils, as_parameters):
+    model = nn.ModuleDict({"attn": _attention_layer(as_parameters=as_parameters)})
+
+    quant_utils.reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model)
+
+    assert _scales(model["attn"]) == [1.0] * 8
+    assert model["attn"]._k_scale_cpu.item() == 1.0 and model["attn"]._v_scale_cpu.item() == 1.0
+
+
+def test_keeps_scales_of_a_kv_cache_scheme(quant_utils):
+    scheme = {"type": "float", "num_bits": 8, "strategy": "tensor", "symmetric": True}
+    model = nn.ModuleDict({"attn": _attention_layer(kv_cache_scheme=scheme)})
+
+    quant_utils.reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model)
+
+    assert _scales(model["attn"]) == pytest.approx([_DUMMY_SCALE] * 8)
+
+
+def test_ignores_layers_without_a_kv_cache_method(quant_utils):
+    model = nn.ModuleDict(
+        {
+            "linear": nn.Linear(4, 4),
+            "other": _attention_layer(method_cls=lambda config: SimpleNamespace(quant_config=config)),
+        }
+    )
+
+    quant_utils.reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model)
+
+    assert _scales(model["other"]) == pytest.approx([_DUMMY_SCALE] * 8)
+
+
+def test_refit_post_processing_resets_the_scales(quant_utils):
+    model = nn.ModuleDict({"attn": _attention_layer()})
+
+    quant_utils.process_quanted_weights_after_loading(model, reload_state={})
+
+    assert _scales(model["attn"]) == [1.0] * 8

     process_fp8_weights_after_loading(reload_state.get("fp8_layers") or [])
     process_mxfp4_moe_weights_after_loading(reload_state.get("mxfp4_moe_modules") or [])
     process_nvfp4_moe_weights_after_loading(reload_state.get("nvfp4_moe_modules") or [])
+    reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model)
     # Last: the rebuild reads ``wo_a``, which is only back in its inference
     # layout once the staged FP8 params above have been reinstated.
     refresh_rocm_attention_weight_caches(model)
 
 
+def reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales(model):
+    """Reset the q/k/v/prob attention scales to 1.0 when the quant config has no KV cache scheme.
+
+    With a compressed-tensors config, vLLM attaches a ``CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod`` to every
+    attention layer even when ``kv_cache_scheme`` is None. ``load_format="dummy"`` fills its
+    q/k/v_scale placeholders with random values, and its ``process_weights_after_loading`` adopts
+    them as the live scales: unlike ``BaseKVCacheMethod``, it has no fallback to 1.0 for scales
+    the checkpoint did not provide. A refit sends no attention scales and re-processes only the
+    linear/MoE layers, so with ``kv_cache_dtype="fp8"`` the rollout keeps quantizing Q/K/V with
+    those random scales and produces garbage.
+
+    Configs that do carry a ``kv_cache_scheme`` are left untouched.
+    """
+    try:
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention.attention import set_default_quant_scales
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.kv_cache import BaseKVCacheMethod
+    except ImportError:
+        return
+    for module in model.modules():
+        quant_method = getattr(module, "quant_method", None)
+        if not isinstance(quant_method, BaseKVCacheMethod):
+            continue
+        if getattr(quant_method.quant_config, "kv_cache_scheme", None) is not None:
+            continue
+        # Older vLLM keeps the scales as the placeholder Parameters, which require grad.
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            set_default_quant_scales(module, register_buffer=False)
+
+
 def load_quanted_weights(weights, model_runner, is_drafter=False):
     if is_drafter:
         drafter = getattr(model_runner, "drafter", None)
